name: Kamahl
description: Kamahl is a powerful barbarian pit fighter from the Pardic Mountains of Otaria who bore the Mirari, renounced it for a druid's life in Krosa, and later fought Karona.

description_citations.text: Onslaught: card flavor text (Onslaught, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.
"The Planes of Planechase". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 31 Aug 2009. Archived by the Internet Archive.

summary.text: Kamahl is a powerful barbarian pit fighter from the Pardic Mountains of Otaria who bore the Mirari, renounced it for a druid's life in Krosa, and later fought Karona.

citations.text: "Kamahl". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
Onslaught: card flavor text (Onslaught, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.
"The Planes of Planechase". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 31 Aug 2009. Archived by the Internet Archive.

bio.text: Drawn by the Mirari, Kamahl left the Pardic Mountains and his sister Jeska to make a name in the Cabal's pits, where he befriended Chainer.

citations.text: "Odyssey", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Torment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: He killed a Krosan dragon attacking Cabal City but Kirtar took the credit and the Mirari, starting the Battle for the Mirari.

citations.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kirtar", section "Pit fighter". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: After Chainer lost control of the Mirari, he begged Kamahl to kill him, and Kamahl did and took the Mirari, attaching it to his sword.

citations.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: Dominated by the Mirari, he tried to take all the tribes under his rule and impaled Jeska with the sword, leaving an incurable wound.

citations.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl and the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kamahl", section "Kamahl and the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: Balthor sacrificed himself so Kamahl could flee, and Kamahl struck down Laquatus, left the Mirari-sword in the soil of Krosa and took up a druidic life.

citations.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Onslaught", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: Braids kidnapped Jeska and the Cabal turned her into Phage, and Kamahl led the Krosans in the Nightmare War, allied uneasily with the Cabal against Akroma.

citations.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kamahl", section "Nightmare War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Onslaught (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

bio.text: His Soul Reaper killed Akroma, Phage and Zagorka and fused them into the goddess Karona, and he then led the numena against her in Sanctum.

citations.text: "Kamahl", section "Rebirth of Karona". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kamahl", section "Karona's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Kamahl", section "Karona's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

status.text: Kamahl is dead, welcoming his sister Jeska in a white void, and Krosa's druids remain dedicated to his memory.

citations.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Legacy". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Jeska", section "Planeswalker". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
"Krosa", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl declares he came to the pits to win.
timeline.quote: I didn't come to play. I came to win.

citation.text: Kamahl, Pit Fighter (Odyssey, 2001), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Balthor travels with Jeska to Cabal City to find Kamahl and fights in the pits, without success.
timeline.quote: briefly fighting in the pits alongside her

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "A New Home". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Balthor opposes Kamahl when the Mirari drives him to take over all the tribes; Jeska is mortally wounded and Kamahl comes to his senses.
timeline.quote: Following Jeska's mortal wounding, Kamahl snapped out of the Mirari's influence

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "A New Home". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Balthor and Kamahl are ambushed in Krosa by Cabalists and Order Legionnaires under Laquatus.
timeline.quote: they were ambushed by Cabalists and Order Legionnaires under the influence of Ambassador Laquatus

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "A New Home". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Balthor lets Kamahl flee and sacrifices himself to destroy Burke as it suffocates him.
timeline.quote: Balthor let Kamahl flee into the forest and sacrificed himself

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "A New Home". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Braids hunts Kamahl with five serpent assassins, who slaughter many but are killed by barbarians.
timeline.quote: killed all five of her snakemen

citation.text: "Braids", section "In league with the Patriarch". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer loses control of the Mirari's power in a pit fight against Kamahl; the city is condemned and abandoned.
timeline.quote: the ruined city was completely abandoned by the Cabal

citation.text: "Cabal City", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer and Kamahl form a twelve-win pit partnership, broken when Kamahl refuses the First's order to throw a match.
timeline.quote: so he refused to fight and broke off their partnership

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Caster". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Under the Mirari's influence Kamahl goes berserk, slaying most of his kin and dealing Jeska a horrific blow.
timeline.quote: Kamahl lost control and went berserk, slaying most of his kin and striking a horrific blow against Jeska

citation.text: "Jeska", section "Barbarian". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl, Phage and Akroma fight in the Grand Coliseum; Akroma loses her legs and Kamahl wins.
timeline.quote: After a three-way bout with Kamahl and Akroma in the Grand Coliseum

citation.text: "Jeska", section "Phage". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl's Soul Reaper kills Akroma and Phage and accidentally Zagorka, their essences forming Karona.
timeline.quote: The essence of the three women blended into a new being

citation.text: "Jeska", section "Phage". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl leaves his mountain home for Cabal City to seek wealth and fame as a pit-fighter.
timeline.quote: He left his mountain home to go to Cabal City to earn himself wealth and fame through pit-fighting.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl wins sponsorship and enters the pits, first sees the Mirari and befriends Seton and Chainer.
timeline.quote: He first saw the Mirari when he was shown the fighters' prizes and became obsessed with obtaining them.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills a Krosan dragon attacking Cabal City but Lieutenant Kirtar is credited and takes the Mirari as his prize, starting the Battle for the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kamahl thus began his journey to claim the artifact for himself.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kirtar uses the Mirari to crystallize much of the Order's fortress, including himself and Captain Pianna; Laquatus ends up with the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kirtar used the device to cast a devastating spell that crystallized much of the fortress

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Emperor Aboshan uses the Mirari to cause a tidal wave that devastates northern Otaria while Kamahl trains youths in Breaker Bay.
timeline.quote: Emperor Aboshan used the Mirari to cause a tidal wave that devastated the northern third of Otaria.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl returns to Cabal City, partners with Chainer for a record winning streak and refuses the Patriarch's order to throw a match.
timeline.quote: Kamahl refused, as he wanted to win or lose games by his skill rather than on the whims of match-fixers.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl accompanies Chainer on his ritual shikar and they fight off an ambushing druid and animals.
timeline.quote: Kamahl and Chainer won the fight, but afterward, Kamahl felt a great deal of guilt

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl is badly hurt in the Order's attack on Cabal City and wakes with snakeskin grafted by Chainer using the Mirari; he burns it off.
timeline.quote: To cleanse himself of the additions, Kamahl burnt off his skin and left the hospital

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Mirari drives Chainer mad and warps him into a mass of dementia beasts; dying, he gives the Mirari to Kamahl, who attaches it to his sword.
timeline.quote: As Chainer died, he gave the Mirari to Kamahl

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kirtar competes in the Cabal's largest pit-fight tournament in Cabal City, hoping to win an artifact for the Order to destroy.
timeline.quote: Hoping to claim a powerful artifact for the Order to destroy

citation.text: "Kirtar", section "Pit fighter". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: A Krosan dragon attacks the city, Kirtar leads the defense, and Kamahl kills the dragon, leaving Kirtar to receive the reward.
timeline.quote: Eventually, Kamahl killed the dragon

citation.text: "Kirtar", section "Pit fighter". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer uses the Mirari to heal Kamahl and then to overthrow the Patriarch and exile him to Aphetto.
timeline.quote: he used it to overthrow the Cabal Patriarch and exile him to Aphetto

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Problems in Cabal City". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer is overloaded by the Mirari in a battle with Kamahl, unleashing dementia horrors, and dies.
timeline.quote: he was overwhelmed by his own spell and died.

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Problems in Cabal City". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl attaches the Mirari to his sword and tries to unite the Pardic barbarians by force.
timeline.quote: He attached it to the pommel of his sword and tried to use its power to unite the Pardic barbarians under his rule.

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Problems in Cabal City". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl mortally wounds his sister Jeska with the Mirari-enhanced sword.
timeline.quote: he used his Mirari-enhanced sword to mortally wound Jeska

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Problems in Cabal City". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl plants the Mirari in Krosa; its power soaks into the continent and mutates the inhabitants, driving forest beasts mad.
timeline.quote: it was he who planted the Mirari there thinking that without a wielder the artifact would be harmless.

citation.text: "Mutant", section "Otarian Mutants". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Odyssey storyline begins on Otaria a century after the Phyrexian Invasion, introducing Kamahl as protagonist.
timeline.quote: it introduces Kamahl as a protagonist

citation.text: "Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl leaves the Pardic Mountains and his sister Jeska to make a name for himself, drawn by the Mirari.
timeline.quote: In leaving behind the Pardic Mountains, where age-old territorial skirmishes between the barbarians and dwarves continue to rage on, Kamahl leaves his sister Jeska

citation.text: "Odyssey", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl arrives at Cabal City lured by a mysterious call and befriends Chainer and Seton.
timeline.quote: There he befriends a young cabalist, Chainer , and a centaur from Krosa, Seton

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: A Krosan dragon attacks; Kamahl lands the killing blow but is pinned under the carcass and Kirtar takes the glory and the sphere.
timeline.quote: Despite Kamahl being he who dealt the killing blow, he remains pinned down underneath the carcass, and Kirtar takes the glory instead.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kirtar tries to gain control of the Order with the sphere but its power devastates the city, leaving him and Pianna dead; Turg takes the artifact.
timeline.quote: leaving him and Pianna dead, and the city in ruins.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Laquatus returns to the Mer capital and stokes Aboshan's fears as Llawan challenges his rule; Kamahl settles in Borben.
timeline.quote: Llawan , the estranged empress, appears to challenge Aboshan's rule.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Turg first fights Seton and Kamahl while Laquatus pursues Kirtar across Otaria's northern plains.
timeline.quote: Turg briefly fought them but withdrew at Laquatus's command

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Turg wrestles Seton in Krosa and blinds him nearly with vomited acid before retreating.
timeline.quote: Turg vomited on Seton's face and retreated

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: At the Order's citadel, Turg fights Kamahl, then takes the Mirari from Kirtar but mistakenly hands it to Satas.
timeline.quote: Turg then mistakenly gave the orb to Satas

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Laquatus controls Balthor and forces him to fight Kamahl; Balthor begs to be killed and Kamahl does so, then kills Laquatus.
timeline.quote: Balthor begged Kamahl to end his suffering

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "Balthor the Defiled". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer completes his shikar with Kamahl and sees a vision of Kuberr.
timeline.quote: He also saw a vision of the Cabal's god Kuberr

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer fills the central arena with dementia beasts, routing the Order's attack; Kamahl is seriously injured.
timeline.quote: the Order broke off its attack and fled the city.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer creates Burke for Laquatus and heals Kamahl with snakeskin; Kamahl burns his skin off, ruining their friendship.
timeline.quote: His refusal to accept the Cabal's gifts ruined his and Chainer's friendship.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl confronts and fights Chainer, melting off his artificial arm; Chainer's healing goes wrong and the Mirari overwhelms him.
timeline.quote: the Mirari’s power finally overwhelmed him, replacing Chainer’s entire body with a writhing mass of dementia creatures.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer begs Kamahl to kill him, and Kamahl does; the Mirari passes to Kamahl.
timeline.quote: while the Mirari now passed on to Kamahl.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl and Chainer become friends.
timeline.quote: Kamahl and Chainer quickly become friends.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl, Seton and Laquatus leave after Kirtar, who has the sphere; Chainer resumes training under Skellum.
timeline.quote: Chainer resumes his training as a dementia summoner under his master Skellum

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Mirari returns to the First, who makes it the prize of the Cabal Anniversary Games; Chainer and Kamahl train as a duo; Llawan claims the throne of the seas.
timeline.quote: Aboshan's wife Llawan claims the throne of the seas

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer completes his initiation in Krosa with Kamahl and becomes a full dementia summoner able to master the Mirari; he creates Burke for Laquatus.
timeline.quote: he becomes a full-fledged dementia summoner.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Games become a show for Chainer; he loses control of dementia creatures, who overrun the city; he draws them into himself and is corrupted, and makes Kamahl promise to take the Mirari.
timeline.quote: makes Kamahl promise to take it and keep it safe, away from misuse.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl tearfully witnesses Chainer's death and takes the Mirari as promised.
timeline.quote: Kamahl tearfully witnesses Chainer's death and takes the Mirari, as promised.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Chainer discovers the Mirari and rises through the Cabal, rivaling the Patriarch before his fall; Kamahl befriends him and Laquatus plots to seize the Mer Empire.
timeline.quote: Chainer's Torment presents the tale of Chainer , a Cabal dementia summoner, discovering the Mirari and rising through the ranks of the Cabal

citation.text: "Torment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl once kept a goretusk firebeast as a pet.
timeline.quote: As a youth, Kamahl took one for a pet.

citation.text: Goretusk Firebeast (Judgment, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Jeska says she and Kamahl both come from Balthor's forge.
timeline.quote: My brother and I both come from Balthor's forge.

citation.text: Jeska, Warrior Adept (Judgment, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Balthor's spirit guides Kamahl to the Mirari-sword, then is struck down by it for the last time, bringing Kamahl to his senses.
timeline.quote: Balthor intervened only to be struck by the sword and killed for the last time

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "Balthor the spirit". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl keeps the Mirari safe from others and himself, keeping his promise to a dying Chainer.
timeline.quote: keeps the Mirari safe from others and himself

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Laquatus and Eesha try to obtain the Mirari while Jeska and Balthor try to separate it from Kamahl for fear of its corrupting influence.
timeline.quote: attempt to obtain the potent orb for themselves

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: After politics and war, the Mirari, attached to Kamahl's sword, is implanted through Laquatus's corpse into the Krosan Forest, channeling its magic into the land.
timeline.quote: is implanted through the corpse of Laquatus and into the Krosan Forest

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl keeps his promise to the dying Chainer and takes the Mirari, attaching it to his sword and fighting off challengers on his way home.
timeline.quote: he takes the Mirari orb for safekeeping.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Under the Mirari's influence Kamahl unites the tribes, defeats the Elite Eight with excessive power and plunges the tribes into civil war.
timeline.quote: he proclaims himself champion; many, however, refuse his rule because he has gone mad with power, plunging the tribes into civil war.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Jeska and Balthor decide to steal the Mirari; Jeska knocks Balthor out and fights Kamahl, who strikes her after a false report that she killed Balthor.
timeline.quote: Balthor arrives to clear the misunderstanding, and Kamahl realizes his tragic mistake.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Cabal troops attack the village; the barbarians unite and win, and Kamahl resolves to bring the surviving Jeska to Seton, with Balthor carrying the Mirari sword.
timeline.quote: Kamahl resolves to bring her to his friend Seton , deep in the Krosan forest, to cure her.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Seton agrees to cure Jeska and sends Kamahl to Thriss, who helps him control his strength and desires and commune with nature.
timeline.quote: gives him substantial help in controlling his strength and desires and makes him able to communicate with nature.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl discovers the assailant is Balthor, zombified by Braids, and ends his undeath in tears.
timeline.quote: he is Balthor, zombified by Braids and instructed to kill Laquatus.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills Laquatus with the Mirari sword, its power now bringing growth and peace, and the forest is rejuvenated.
timeline.quote: The merman dies pinned by the sword.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl returns home, is dominated by the Mirari and tries to take all the tribes under his dictatorship, dividing the barbarians.
timeline.quote: Initially, he was content simply to return home covered in glory, but inevitably, the Mirari dominated his mind.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl and the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: In battle Kamahl impales Jeska with the Mirari-sword, leaving an incurable wound; shocked, he resolves to be rid of the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kamahl viciously impaling Jeska with his Mirari-sword

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl and the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Attacked at the edge of the Krosan forest, Balthor sacrifices himself so Kamahl can flee with Jeska; Seton guides Kamahl in and Thriss teaches him druidism.
timeline.quote: Balthor chose to sacrifice himself to let Kamahl flee with Jeska.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Laquatus mind-controls zombified Balthor into fighting Kamahl, who is forced to strike down his old mentor at Balthor's plea.
timeline.quote: Balthor begged Kamahl to end his torment, and so Kamahl was forced to strike down his old mentor.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl strikes down Laquatus with the Mirari-sword, leaves it in the ground and forsakes the Mirari for a druidic life.
timeline.quote: With that act, Kamahl forsook the Mirari and his violent past

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Braids kidnaps Jeska, and the Cabal Patriarch turns her into Phage; Kamahl and Phage fight until Akroma interrupts and they defeat her together.
timeline.quote: who tried to kill her, but instead turned her into Phage

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills Laquatus in Krosa and leaves the Mirari-sword in the ground.
timeline.quote: Kamahl finishing the merman by driving the Mirari-sword through Laquatus and into the ground

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: The Mirari falls into Kamahl's hands, and his actions inadvertently lead to the Rebirth of Karona.
timeline.quote: saw it eventually falling into the hands of Kamahl , whose actions inadvertently led to the Rebirth of Karona

citation.text: "Rift Era", section "Rise and Fall of Karona". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl leaves his violent former life behind.
timeline.quote: Kamahl left the violence of his former life behind him

citation.text: Tribal Unity (Onslaught, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Krosa unleashes peace in Kamahl and Kamahl unleashes fury in Krosa.
timeline.quote: As Krosa unleashed the peace in Kamahl, he unleashed the fury in Krosa.

citation.text: Kamahl's Summons (Onslaught, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Akroma attacks Phage in the Grand Coliseum, but Kamahl interferes and Phage's touch maims Akroma's legs.
timeline.quote: Akroma had to flee, grievously wounded and maimed as her legs fell victim to Phage's touch.

citation.text: "Akroma", section "Angel of Wrath". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl thrusts the Mirari into the Krosan forest, mutating Otaria's people.
timeline.quote: the barbarian Kamahl thrust the Mirari

citation.text: "Dominaria (plane)", section "Coming of Karona". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl declares war on Ixidor and leads the Cabal and Krosan alliance against Topos in the Nightmare War, defeating his Mirari-possessed persona.
timeline.quote: Kamahl led the joint forces into battle

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Nightmare War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Deathwurms are purged from Phage, but Kamahl must watch his sister become Phage again to bind them.
timeline.quote: was forced to watch his sister become Phage once again.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Nightmare War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

timeline.summary: Kamahl meditates in Krosa for a year until Stonebrow revives him with the Soul Reaper.
timeline.quote: Green energy flowed from Soul Reaper to Kamahl, who was revitalized

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Nightmare War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
